resolution: The stall watchdog + a bench against the user's real 4,886-piece map (live world snapshot) split the remaining time. JS passes are all fast now: footprints 14ms uncached/0ms cached, liftToTerrain 3ms, joinKeys 50ms, move-ghost update 2ms/event, 179-remove fold 8ms — and the new move probe showed move->standing at 210ms JS-side. The 1-2s frame stalls (2091/1342/1055) are therefore HOST-side: ~4,886 retained Scene3D.Mesh nodes, and a 179-piece move unmounts+remounts ~1,800 of them in one update — per-node host work at that scale is the seconds. That is exactly the already-approved static-instance renderer work (hmsc_massive_scale_caps / react-3d-is-authoring); piecemeal JS fixes can't move it further. One last app-side waste fixed in ce5d5a47a: setMoveDelta pushed a fresh {dx,dz} per raw mouse event even when the cell-snapped delta hadn't changed, re-rendering the pane + rebuilding the 179-piece ghost while the drag sat inside one cell — now skipped (same no-op class as the paint fix). Note: the 2091ms stall at the top of the user's log sits right after a PaintCanvas mount (layer switch) — that's the known StaticSurface chunk re-bake cost, separate from the move. Bench scratch at zig-out/game/bench/move-stall.ts (gitignored).
